body.p: This amendment responds to the final office action mailed September 18. In the final office action the Examiner:
" rejected claims 1, 3, 5, 8-10, 12, and 15-20 under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable
over Nakamura et al. (US 2019/0298202 Al), in view of Varcoe et al. (US
2019/0133478 Al), and Ishiyama et al. (US 2005/0192502 Al);
" rejected claims 2, 11, 14, and 21 under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over
Nakamura, in view of Varcoe and Ishiyama as applied to claims 1, 8, and 15
respectively, above, and further in view of Ledbetter et al. (US 2020/0256929 Al);
" rejected claim 13 under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Nakamura, in view
of Varcoe as applied to claim 8 above, and further in view of Zuckerman et al. (US
" objected to claims 4 and 6 as being dependent upon a rejected base claim, but would
be allowable if rewritten in independent form; and
" allowed claim 22.

Applicant's attorneys thank Primary Examiner Mattson for the opportunity to discuss the application during a telephone interview on November 26, 2024 with Douglas Crisman and Ai Leen Koh ("Interview 1"), and in a follow-up interview on November 26, 2024 with Ai Leen Koh ("Interview 2").

In Interview 1, the Applicant's attorneys and the Examiner discussed the rejection of claim 1 under 35 U.S.C. 103. The Examiner explained the rationale for combining Nakamura and Ishiyama and suggested agreed that further amendments to clarify the spacing or arrangement of the sensors. No specific agreement was reached.
In Interview 2, the Applicant's attorneys and the Examiner discussed a proposed

amendment to claim 1 to add features from paragraph 189 of the specification. The Examiner indicated that the proposed amendment would advance prosecution but would require further search and consideration. Claim 1 has been amended accordingly. Analogous amendments have been made to independent claim 15.
Claims 1, 15, and 16 have been amended. Support for the amendments can be found in at least paragraphs [0189] of the application as filed. No new matter has been added.
With respect to all amendments, Applicant has not dedicated or abandoned any

unclaimed subject matter. Moreover, Applicant has not acquiesced to any characterizations of the invention, nor any rejections or objections of the claims, made by the Examiner. Moreover, the Applicant hereby rescinds any prior disclaimer of claim scope, to the extent they exist, made during the prosecution of this application or made during the prosecution of any patent or other related patents/applications, and advises the Examiner that any such previous disclaimers and the cited references that they were made to avoid may need to be revisited.
After entry of this amendment, the pending claims are: claims 1-6 and 8-22.
I. REJECTION OF CLAIMS 1, 3, 5, 8-10, 12, AND 15-20 UNDER 35 U.S.C. 103 AS BEING
UNPATENTABLE OVER NAKAMURA, IN VIEW OF VARCOE AND ISHIYAMA
As amended, independent claims 1 and 15 each requires:
the plurality of magnetometers are spatially distributed such
that (i) in Fourier space the plurality of magnetometers have a wavevector coverage to recover information from both the
biomagnetic field from the subject's organ and the
body.h1: background magnetic field and (ii) the plurality of
body.p: magnetometers have respective spacings that are configured to
maximize a common mode variance for one or more sources
of the background magnetic field while minimizing the
common mode variance for the subject's organ;
See, e.g., claim 1 (emphasis added) Support for the claim amendments can be found in paragraph 189 of the application as filed, reproduced below:
[0189] The right image in panel ii of Figure 4F shows a schematic
of two sensor layers indicating dimensions and gradiometric baseline. In the example shown in panel ii of Figure 4F, the
housing 251 includes a two-layer scalar OPM array that includes five pairs of commercial magnetometers, arranged as shown. To
ensure a high common-mode rejection ratio (CMRR), the
magnetometers were paired as gradiometers with a baseline in the
direction normal to the sensor array plane. The sensor spacings
were chosen to maximize the common mode variance for distant
noise sources while minimizing that variance for nearby signal
sources.
The cited combination of Nakamura, Varcoe, and Ishiyama does not disclose or
suggest a plurality of magnetometers having "respective spacings that are configured to
maximize a common mode variance for one or more sources of the background magnetic
body.h1: field while minimizing the common mode variance for the subject's organ" re recited in the
body.p: amended independent claims.
Furthermore, as noted in the Substance of Interview, the Examiner agreed that the
amended claims further require search and consideration.
Thus, for at least the above reasons, amended claims 1 and 15 and their associated
dependent claims 3, 5, 8-10, 12, and 16-20 are patentable over the cited combination of
Nakamura, Varcoe, and Ishiyama.
Applicant respectfully requests that these rejections be withdrawn.
II. REJECTION OF CLAIMS 2, 11, 14, AND 21 UNDER 35 U.S.C. 103 AS BEING UNPATENTABLE
OVER NAKAMURA, IN VIEW OF VARCOE AND ISHIYAMA AS APPLIED TO CLAIMS 1, 8, AND
15 RESPECTIVELY, ABOVE, AND FURTHER IN VIEW OF LEDBETTER
Claims 2, 11, 14, and 21 depend from respective independent claims 1 and 15, and

thus they include all the features of the independent claims by virtue of their dependency. As discussed above, Nakamura, Varcoe, and Ishiyama do not teach or suggest all the features of the amended independent claims. Furthermore, Ledbetter is not cited for, and does not teach,
the features of the amended independent claims that are missing from Nakamura, Varcoe, and
Ishiyama. Thus, claims 2, 11, 14, and 21 are patentable over the cited combination of
Nakamura, Varcoe, Ishiyama, and Ledbetter.
Applicant respectfully requests that these rejections be withdrawn.
III. REJECTION OF CLAIM 13 UNDER 35 U.S.C. 103 AS BEING UNPATENTABLE OVER
NAKAMURA, IN VIEW OF VARCOE AS APPLIED TO CLAIM 8 ABOVE, AND FURTHER IN
Claim 13 depends from claim 1 and thus it includes all the features of the independent
claim by virtue of its dependency. As discussed above, Nakamura, Varcoe, and Ishiyama do
not teach or suggest all the features of amended claim 1. Furthermore, Zuckerman is not cited
for, and does not teach, the features of amended claim 1 that are missing from Nakamura,
Varcoe, and Ishiyama. Thus, claim 13 is patentable over the cited combination of Nakamura,
Varcoe, Ishiyama, and Zuckerman.
Applicant respectfully requests that these rejections be withdrawn.
IV. OBJECTION TO CLAIMS 4 AND 6 AS BEING DEPENDENT UPON A REJECTED BASE CLAIM,
body.h1: BUT WOULD BE ALLOWABLE IF REWRITTEN IN INDEPENDENT FORM
body.p: The Applicant thanks the Examiner for indicating the allowability of claims 4 and 6.
In this Response, the Applicant has not rewritten these claims in independent form because
the Applicant has amended independent claims 1 and 15 in another way.
V. ALLOWANCE OF CLAIM 22
The Applicant thanks the Examiner for noting the allowance of claim 22.

By responding in the foregoing remarks only to particular positions asserted by the Examiner, the Applicants do not necessarily acquiesce in other positions that have not been explicitly addressed. In addition, the Applicants' arguments for the patentability of a claim should not be understood as implying that no other reasons for the patentability of that claim exist.

In light of the above amendments and remarks, the Applicants respectfully request that the Examiner reconsider this application with a view towards allowance. The Examiner is invited to call the undersigned attorney at (650) 843-4000, if a telephone call could help resolve any remaining items.
Respectfully submitted,
